note: Player copy for the guided designer. Step ids match DesignerStep. Check codes match StepperChecks and FailureKind. Every string has a stable id. Simple is the kid voice. Engineer cites the units and formulas. Live numbers stay in the readout.

goal.text: Pick the job. What are we carrying, and where is it going?

kid.text: The cargo decides the rocket. A small box and a heavy satellite need different ships.

engineer.text: Cargo mass is in kg. The trip asks for a change in speed, Δv, in m/s.

pass.text: The job is set. Next you build a rocket that can do it.

goal.text: Choose a mission, a payload, and a target orbit. Payload mass (kg) and the required Δv (m/s) come from that job.

kid.text: What you carry, and how far it goes, decide how big the rocket must be.

engineer.text: Payload mass (kg), volume (m³), and maxG come from the mission. A hit is altitude within ±5%, inclination within ±0.5°, or the required Δv (m/s) reached.

pass.text: Payload and orbit are set. The required Δv (m/s) is now a real target.

goal.text: Give it a shove strong enough to leave the ground.

kid.text: If the push is weaker than the weight, the rocket stays on the pad. A little extra shove gets it climbing.

engineer.text: Liftoff TWR = F/(m·g0), with g0 = 9.80665 m/s². The step passes at TWR ≥ 1.3 and blocks below 1.0.

pass.text: It can lift off. The shove beats the weight with room to spare.

goal.text: Lift off with TWR ≥ 1.3. TWR = F/(m·g0) and g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

kid.text: A rocket that only just equals its weight barely moves. Extra push makes the climb quick and honest.

engineer.text: TWR = F/(m·g0), g0 = 9.80665 m/s². Pass at ≥ 1.3; red below 1.0. Isp drops 0.6% per 1% mixture offset, and ±6% is the sputter line. Overpressure λ = 0.02·max(0, pc/pc_rated−1)² per second.

pass.text: Liftoff TWR ≥ 1.3. TWR = F/(m·g0), g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

goal.text: Pack enough fuel to finish the whole trip.

kid.text: Fuel is how the rocket gets its speed. Too little, and it runs out before the job is done.

engineer.text: You need Δv margin ≥ 0, in m/s. The air-push limit is q_lim = 35 kPa·(SF/1.4)·(σ_y/500). Above 0.85·q_lim the walls are working hard.

pass.text: You have enough speed for this trip.

goal.text: Reach the orbit with Δv margin ≥ 0. Margin is leftover speed divided by the speed the mission needs.

kid.text: Empty tanks mean the trip stops short. Thick enough walls keep the rocket whole when the air pushes hardest.

engineer.text: Δv margin ≥ 0 means total Δv (m/s) covers the mission. Wall thickness t = SF·p_t·r/σ_y. q_lim = 35 kPa·(SF/1.4)·(σ_y/500). Amber when max-Q > 0.85·q_lim. Stages collide if v_rel < 0.5 + 0.02·q_kPa m/s within 2 s.

pass.text: Δv margin ≥ 0. Total speed (m/s) covers the mission, and max-Q is within 0.85·q_lim.

goal.text: Keep the pointy end forward, and make sure the cargo fits.

kid.text: A rocket that is heavy at the wrong end flips over. The nose has to be roomy enough for the cargo.

engineer.text: The cargo fits when its volume ≤ π(0.45·D_f)²·0.8·L_f and its diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f. It tumbles if S < 0 and CAR < 1.

pass.text: The cargo fits, and the rocket stays pointy-end up.

goal.text: Fit the payload in the fairing, and keep S ≥ 0 with CAR ≥ 1 so it does not tumble.

kid.text: Pointy-end up is a balance trick. The nose also has to swallow the cargo with room to spare.

engineer.text: Fit: volume ≤ π(0.45·D_f)²·0.8·L_f and diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f. S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D. CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero at α = 4°. Tumble when S < 0 and CAR < 1 for 0.5 s, or α > 15° at q > 20 kPa.

pass.text: Fairing fit passes, and S and CAR stay off the tumble line. S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D.

goal.text: Throw it away, or bring the booster home.

kid.text: Coming home uses fuel you saved on purpose. Legs keep it from tipping over at the end.

engineer.text: A pad return needs about 2·v_h m/s of speed change. A barge needs about 0.3·v_h. Legs fold if the sink speed v_z is above v_leg.

pass.text: The landing fuel covers the trip home.

goal.text: Expend the booster, or land it. A required landing needs reserve ≥ Δv_land, in m/s.

kid.text: Saving a little fuel is what makes a landing possible. Without legs, it falls over at the end.

engineer.text: RTLS boostback Δv ≈ 2·v_h(MECO). Barge Δv ≈ 0.3·v_h(MECO). Δv_land ≈ v_term + g·t_burn·(1 − 1/TWR_land). Light legs take v_z ≤ 2 m/s; heavy legs ≤ 4 m/s.

pass.text: Landing reserve (m/s) covers Δv_land. Pad ≈ 2·v_h, barge ≈ 0.3·v_h.

goal.text: Paint it and name it. Colors do not change the flight.

kid.text: Paint is just for you. The rocket flies the same in any color.

engineer.text: Paint, accent, and name are not in the mass or drag sums. Δv (m/s), TWR, and q_lim (kPa) stay put.

pass.text: Paint and a name. This does not change how it flies.

goal.text: Set paint, accent, and name. Livery does not change Δv (m/s), TWR, or q_lim (kPa).

kid.text: A name and a color make it yours. They do not add weight or push.

engineer.text: No mass, aero, or propulsion term reads the livery. Δv (m/s), TWR = F/(m·g0), and q_lim (kPa) are unchanged.

pass.text: Livery is cosmetic. Δv (m/s), TWR, and q_lim (kPa) do not move.

goal.text: Look at what might go wrong, then fly.

kid.text: You see the risks before you launch. A surprise you were not told about is not part of this game.

engineer.text: The risk list comes from a preview flight. Red means a limit is already crossed, such as q > q_lim (kPa).

pass.text: No red risks. Ready to launch.

goal.text: Read every predicted risk, then launch. A red risk means a limit is already crossed, such as q > q_lim.

kid.text: The list is the flight being honest with you. If something is likely to break, it says so here.

engineer.text: Predict mode lists each failure kind with its margin. Triggers include q > q_lim, S < 0 and CAR < 1, and pc above pc_rated. Random kinds are seeded by the design hash and the mission seed. Gentle mode turns those random kinds off.

pass.text: No red risk is on the list. q is within q_lim (kPa), and the other failure triggers are clear.
A cargo is chosen.

red.text: Pick a cargo first. The cargo decides the rocket.

fix.text: Choose what this rocket is carrying.

pass.text: payload.type is set, so mass (kg) and volume (m³) are known.

red.text: payload.type is empty, so mass (kg) and the Δv (m/s) budget are unknown.

fix.text: Set payload.type. Mass (kg) and maxG come from that payload.

pass.text: The cargo has a place to go.

red.text: Pick where this cargo is going.

fix.text: Choose the trip: how high, or which path around Earth.

pass.text: payload.orbit is set. The required Δv is in m/s.

red.text: payload.orbit is empty, so the required Δv (m/s) cannot be checked.

fix.text: Set payload.orbit. A hit is altitude within ±5%, or inclination within ±0.5°.

pass.text: The numbers for this rocket worked out.

red.text: We couldn't work this rocket out. Try one smaller change, then check again.

fix.text: Undo the last odd change, or start again from a starter rocket.

pass.text: Liftoff TWR and Δv (m/s) both came back as real numbers.

red.text: Liftoff TWR or the Δv margin did not come back as a real number.

fix.text: Check engine count, propellant mass (kg), and that every stage can be summed into TWR = F/(m·g0).

pass.text: The shove is stronger than the weight. It can leave the pad.

red.text: Too heavy to lift off. Add engines on the bottom, or take fuel off.

fix.text: Add engines on the first stage, or take some fuel off.

pass.text: Liftoff TWR = F/(m·g0) ≥ 1.0, with g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

red.text: Liftoff TWR < 1.0. F < m·g0, so it cannot climb. g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

fix.text: Raise first-stage thrust F, or cut liftoff mass m, until TWR > 1.0. Aim for ≥ 1.3.

pass.text: The shove is strong enough for a clean liftoff.

amber.text: Slow off the pad. A bit more push helps.

fix.text: Add an engine, or take a little fuel off, so it jumps off the pad.

pass.text: Liftoff TWR ≥ 1.3. TWR = F/(m·g0), g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

amber.text: Liftoff TWR is at least 1.0 and below 1.3. Gravity losses (m/s) climb when the rise is this slow.

fix.text: Add thrust or shed mass until TWR ≥ 1.3.

pass.text: Every stage has an engine.

red.text: A stage has no engines. Give it at least one.

fix.text: Put at least one engine on every stage that flies.

pass.text: engineCount ≥ 1 on every stage, so thrust F is defined and TWR = F/(m·g0) can be above 0.

red.text: engineCount < 1. Thrust F is 0, so TWR = F/(m·g0) is 0.

fix.text: Set engineCount ≥ 1. TWR needs a real thrust F.

pass.text: The engines fit under the stage.

red.text: Too many engines for this width. Use fewer, or make the stage wider.

fix.text: Use fewer engines, or make the bottom of the rocket wider.

pass.text: The cluster fits the stage diameter. Exit diameter grows with √ε.

red.text: The engine exits do not fit the stage diameter. Exit diameter grows with √ε.

fix.text: Lower engineCount, widen the stage (m), or pick a smaller ε so the exits pack.

pass.text: The bottom engines can push in the thick air.

red.text: This bottom engine only works up high. Use one that pushes at the pad.

fix.text: Put a ground engine on the first stage.

pass.text: The pad stage has sea-level thrust, so F_SL > 0. Isp_SL = Isp_vac − p_a·A_e/(ṁ·g0).

red.text: Sea-level thrust is 0. Isp_SL = Isp_vac − p_a·A_e/(ṁ·g0) has collapsed for this bell at the pad.

fix.text: Use an engine with F_SL > 0 on the liftoff stage. A vacuum ε belongs upstairs.

pass.text: The engine layout matches how many engines you have.

red.text: That engine layout needs a different number of engines.

fix.text: Change how many engines you have, or pick a layout that matches.

pass.text: engineCount matches the pattern, so the exits pack. Exit diameter grows with √ε.

red.text: The cluster pattern has a fixed engine count, and engineCount does not match, so the pack of exits (∝ √ε) is wrong.

fix.text: Set engineCount to the pattern's count, or choose auto. Exit diameter grows with √ε.

pass.text: The engines sit inside the width of the stage.

amber.text: The engines stick out past the edge. Make the stage a bit wider.

fix.text: Widen the stage, or use a tighter engine layout.

pass.text: Stage diameter covers the exits. Exit diameter grows with √ε.

amber.text: Stage diameter is under the layout's minimum. Exit diameter grows with √ε, so a wide bell needs a wider stage.

fix.text: Increase stage diameter (m), or reduce ε, until the body covers the exits.

pass.text: Each engine's bell is one this game knows.

red.text: That engine bell is not on the list. Pick another.

fix.text: Choose a bell from the list for that engine.

pass.text: The nozzle id is in the engine list, so ε and A_e are known.

red.text: The nozzle id is missing from the engine list, so ε and Isp_SL cannot be computed.

fix.text: Pick a listed nozzle. Isp_SL depends on ε through A_e = ε·A_t.

pass.text: The upper stages push hard enough to keep climbing.

amber.text: An upper stage pushes gently. A stronger engine helps it finish.

fix.text: Give the upper stage a stronger engine, or lighten what it carries.

pass.text: Upper-stage vacuum TWR is above the gentle-push line.

amber.text: Upper-stage TWR_vac is low. TWR = F_vac/(m·g0), with g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

fix.text: Raise upper-stage thrust, or cut the mass above it, so TWR_vac climbs.

pass.text: The fuel mix is close to the normal recipe.

amber.text: The fuel mix is too far off. Put it back near the normal mix.

red.text: The mix is so far off an engine may sputter and quit. Slide it back.

fix.text: Move the mix back to the middle. A little off is fine, and a lot is not.

pass.text: Mixture offset is inside ±6%. Isp falls 0.6% per 1% off nominal.

amber.text: Mixture offset is outside ±6%. That is the sputter line. Isp is already down 0.6% per 1%.

red.text: bad-mixture can quench the burn once the offset passes ±6%. Isp penalty is −0.6% per 1% off nominal.

fix.text: Set the mixture offset back inside ±6% of the catalog mixture ratio.

pass.text: The engines are running inside their safe push.

amber.text: The burn is running hot. That can pop an engine.

red.text: An engine is past its safe limit and can burst. Turn the pressure down.

fix.text: Lower how hard the engine burns until it is back in the safe range.

pass.text: pc ≤ pc_rated, so the overpressure hazard λ is 0.

amber.text: pc > pc_rated. Hazard λ = 0.02·max(0, pc/pc_rated−1)² per second.

red.text: engine-overpressure when pc > 1.15·pc_rated. λ = 0.02·max(0, pc/pc_rated−1)² per second.

fix.text: Lower pc toward pc_rated. Thrust F ∝ pc, so the hazard falls faster than the thrust.

pass.text: If one engine stops, the others can still lift you.

amber.text: If one engine stops, you would sink. Add a spare.

red.text: One engine quitting would end the flight. More engines, and a backup set of controls, let you ride it out.

fix.text: Add engines on that stage. A backup set of controls helps you survive one quitting.

pass.text: Losing one engine leaves TWR_after > 1. N ≥ 7 with redundant avionics survives one out if TWR_after > 1.05.

amber.text: TWR with n−1 engines is under 1.0, so an engine-out cannot climb. g0 = 9.80665 m/s².

red.text: engine-out is survived only when N ≥ 7, avionics are redundant, and TWR_after > 1.05.

fix.text: Add engines until N ≥ 7 and TWR_after > 1.05, and set avionics to redundant.

pass.text: Every stage has fuel.

red.text: A stage has no fuel. Add some.

fix.text: Load fuel on every stage that has to burn.

pass.text: propMass > 0 on every stage, so Δv (m/s) can be computed.

red.text: propMass is 0. That stage's Δv is 0 m/s.

fix.text: Set propMass > 0. Δv (m/s) needs propellant in the rocket equation.

pass.text: You have enough speed for this trip.

amber.text: You will just make it. A little more fuel gives room to spare.

red.text: Not enough speed for this trip. Add fuel, or lighten the cargo.

fix.text: Add fuel, drop a little cargo, or add a stage.

pass.text: Δv margin ≥ 0. Total Δv (m/s) covers the mission need.

amber.text: Δv margin is thin but not negative. Speed is in m/s.

red.text: Δv margin < 0. The shortfall is in m/s against the mission's required Δv.

fix.text: Add propellant, cut payload mass (kg), or add a stage until margin ≥ 0.

pass.text: The hardest air push stays inside what the walls can take.

amber.text: The air pushes hard on the tanks. A thicker wall, or less push low down, helps.

fix.text: Thicken the walls, or ease the climb while the air is still thick.
Raise SF, pick a higher σ_y, or lower maxQThrottle so q stays under q_lim.

pass.text: The top stage does its share of the work.

amber.text: The top stage does little work. Give it more fuel.

fix.text: Add fuel to the top stage so it can finish the trip.

pass.text: The top stage's Δv is a fair share of total Δv (m/s).

amber.text: Top-stage Δv is a small fraction of total Δv (m/s).

fix.text: Move propellant mass onto the upper stage to raise its Δv (m/s).

pass.text: The tanks can hold this cold fuel.

amber.text: This fuel is far too cold for these tanks. Pick a metal tank.

fix.text: Switch the cold fuel's tank to a material that can take the cold.

pass.text: The tank material has cryoOK, or the propellant is not cryogenic.

amber.text: Cryogenic propellant in a material with cryoOK false. That is a hard fail at T+0.

fix.text: Change material to one with cryoOK true, or pick a storable propellant.

pass.text: This rocket is put together in a way the game can fly.

red.text: Something in the build does not fit together. Start from a starter rocket and change one thing.

fix.text: Go back to a starter rocket, then change one piece at a time.

pass.text: The design matches the schema, so mass (kg) and Δv (m/s) can be summed.

red.text: The design failed the schema, so TWR and Δv (m/s) cannot be formed.

fix.text: Fix the stage fields the schema rejected. Counts, diameters (m), and masses (kg) have to be real numbers.

pass.text: Each stage sits happily on the one below it.

red.text: One stage is much wider than the one under it. Make it narrower.

fix.text: Narrow the upper stage, or widen the one below it.

pass.text: Upper diameter stays within 1.6 times the stage below (m), so Cd0 does not pick up a surprise shoulder.

red.text: An upper stage is wider than 1.6 times the stage below (m). That shoulder feeds Cd0.

fix.text: Cut the upper diameter (m), or raise the lower one, until the ratio is at most 1.6 and Cd0 stays honest.

pass.text: The joints between stages match their widths.

amber.text: A joint between stages does not match their widths. That can make the rocket less steady.

fix.text: Let the joint follow the widths. Wider at the bottom when the bottom stage is wider.

pass.text: Interstage shape matches the diameter step. Drag includes ΣdragDeltaCd_interstage in Cd0.

amber.text: Interstage shape disagrees with the diameters (m). A shoulder, wider on top, pulls the nose off the wind. Cd0 includes ΣdragDeltaCd_interstage.

fix.text: Set the joint to match the two diameters (m). Cd0 includes ΣdragDeltaCd_interstage.

pass.text: The fuel lasts to the end of the job.

amber.text: The fuel is tight. You might run out before the job is done.

red.text: A stage runs out of fuel before the trip is done. Load more, or add a stage.

fix.text: Add fuel, or add a stage, so the burn lasts to the target.

pass.text: No stage empties below the target. Δv margin ≥ 0, in m/s.

amber.text: Propellant is close to empty before the required Δv (m/s) is done.

red.text: prop-depletion: a stage empties below the target, so delivered Δv (m/s) falls short.

fix.text: Add propellant mass (kg), or a stage, until Δv margin ≥ 0.

pass.text: The walls can take the hardest push from the air.

amber.text: The air is pushing close to what the walls can take. Thicker walls, or a gentler climb, help.

red.text: The air would bend this rocket. Thicker walls, a tougher material, or a gentler climb fixes it.

fix.text: Make the walls stronger, pick a tougher material, or ease off low in the climb.

pass.text: q ≤ q_lim and MS = F_allow/F − 1 ≥ 0. q_lim = 35 kPa·(SF/1.4)·(σ_y/500).

amber.text: max-Q is above 0.85·q_lim. q_lim = 35 kPa·(SF/1.4)·(σ_y/500). MS = F_allow/F − 1 is getting thin.

red.text: structural-maxq when MS < 0 or q > q_lim. q_lim = 35 kPa·(SF/1.4)·(σ_y/500). F_allow = σ_y·2πr·t/SF + p_t·πr².

fix.text: Raise SF, pick a higher σ_y, or lower maxQThrottle so q stays under q_lim.

pass.text: The push stays gentle enough for the cargo and the rocket.

amber.text: The climb is getting rough. Ease off before something breaks.

red.text: The shove would crush the cargo or break the rocket. Ease off on the way up.

fix.text: Ease off during the hard part, or set a gentler limit on the shove.

pass.text: Acceleration stays under min(payload maxG, 8 g).

amber.text: Peak g is close to min(maxG, 8 g). Over-g fires above that.

red.text: overg when a > min(maxG, 8 g). Above 8 g the vehicle breaks up.

fix.text: Lower gLimit so acceleration stays under maxG and under 8 g.

pass.text: The tanks can take this cold fuel.

amber.text: Cold fuel in the wrong tank is a bad match. Pick a tank that can take the cold.

red.text: The tanks would crack on the pad. This fuel is far too cold for that material.

fix.text: Change the tank to a material that can take the cold.

pass.text: cryoOK is true for this propellant, so there is no T+0 material fail.

amber.text: A cryogenic propellant is paired with a material near cryoOK false.

red.text: cryo-material is a hard fail at T+0 when cryogenic propellant sits in a material with cryoOK false.

fix.text: Set the tank material to one with cryoOK true.

pass.text: The stages move apart cleanly.

amber.text: The stages might bump when they split. Give them a firmer push apart.

red.text: The stages would bump and then flip. Push them apart harder.

fix.text: Use a stronger push apart when the stages split.

pass.text: v_rel stays above 0.5 + 0.02·q_kPa m/s in the 2 s after separation.

amber.text: Separation speed is near the collision line, v_rel < 0.5 + 0.02·q_kPa m/s.

red.text: separation-collision when v_rel < 0.5 + 0.02·q_kPa (m/s) within 2 s. Hot staging without a vent also fails.

fix.text: Raise sepImpulse so v_rel clears 0.5 + 0.02·q_kPa m/s. Hot staging needs a vented interstage.

pass.text: The nose is wide enough for the stage under it.

red.text: The nose is much thinner than the stage under it. Make the nose wider.

fix.text: Widen the nose so it matches the stage.

pass.text: Fairing diameter is at least half the top-stage diameter, and payload diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f.

red.text: D_f is under half the top-stage diameter. The fit rule also needs payload diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f.

fix.text: Raise D_f (m) until it covers the stage, and keep payload diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f.

pass.text: The nose widens gently above the stage.

amber.text: The nose flares out a lot above the stage. Try a wider stage or a smaller nose.

fix.text: Make the nose a bit narrower, or the stage under it wider. The cargo still has to fit inside it.

pass.text: Barrel diameter D_f over top-stage diameter D_s is at most the flare ratio, and the shoulder half angle is under the flare angle limit (designer-limits fairingFlare).

amber.text: D_f / D_s is over warnRatio, or the shoulder half angle is over warnAngleDeg. Above that the shoulder is closer to a ledge than a cone.

fix.text: Lower D_f (m), or raise the top-stage diameter. Keep payload diameter at or under 0.9 D_f.

pass.text: The cargo fits in the nose.

red.text: The cargo doesn't fit in the nose. Make the nose longer or wider.

fix.text: Make the nose longer or wider until the cargo fits.

pass.text: Payload volume ≤ π(0.45·D_f)²·0.8·L_f and diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f.

red.text: Fairing fit failed. Volume must be ≤ π(0.45·D_f)²·0.8·L_f, and diameter ≤ 0.9·D_f.

fix.text: Increase D_f or L_f until both fit checks pass.

pass.text: The nose is lighter than the cargo.

amber.text: The nose weighs more than the cargo. A shorter or lighter nose helps.

fix.text: Use a shorter nose, or a lighter one.

pass.text: Fairing mass (kg) is under payload mass (kg).

amber.text: Fairing mass exceeds payload mass. That mass still has to be lifted, so Δv (m/s) falls.

fix.text: Shorten L_f, or pick a lighter fairing, so fairing mass (kg) drops.

pass.text: The rocket wants to stay pointy-end up.

amber.text: This rocket is wobbly. Add fins, or put the heavy parts higher.

red.text: Your rocket would flip. Add fins, or put the heavy parts higher.

fix.text: Add fins, or move weight toward the nose.

pass.text: Liftoff S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D stays pointy-end forward, or the pad stage is steered and CAR can cover it.

amber.text: S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D is soft. A steered pad stage can still fly if CAR stays at least 1.

red.text: Unguided S < 0, or S < 0 and CAR < 1. CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero at α = 4°.

fix.text: Add fin area so x_cp moves back, or move mass forward. S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D and CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero.

pass.text: The fins are strong, and the rocket can still turn.

amber.text: Very steady, maybe too steady to turn well. Try smaller fins.

fix.text: Make the fins a little smaller so it can still turn.

pass.text: S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D is inside the useful band, so it can still turn at α = 4°.

amber.text: S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D is past about 4 calibers, so it weathercocks. CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero at α = 4° gets harder to use.

fix.text: Reduce fin area so x_cp moves forward and S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D drops. CAR stays M_ctrl/M_aero.

pass.text: The rocket stays pointy-end up through the thick air.

amber.text: It is close to flipping. Bigger fins, or a gentler turn, keep the nose forward.

red.text: Your rocket would flip in the thick air. Add fins, or put the heavy parts higher.

fix.text: Add fins, let the engines steer more, or move weight up.

pass.text: S ≥ 0 or CAR ≥ 1. S = (x_cg − x_cp)/D. CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero at α = 4°.

amber.text: S and CAR are near the tumble line. Tumble when S < 0 and CAR < 1 for 0.5 s, or α > 15° at q > 20 kPa.

red.text: Tumble when S < 0 and CAR < 1 for 0.5 s, or α > 15° at q > 20 kPa.

fix.text: Increase fin area or gimbal δ so CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero rises, and move mass forward so S ≥ 0.

pass.text: The ride is gentle enough for this cargo.

amber.text: Too bumpy for this cargo. Ease the push on the way up.

red.text: This ride is too rough for people. Ease the push so it stays gentle.

fix.text: Ease the climb, or set a gentler limit on how hard it can shove.

pass.text: Peak acceleration stays under payload maxG.

amber.text: Peak a > payload maxG. Over-g is a > min(maxG, 8 g).

red.text: A crewed payload blocks when peak g exceeds maxG. The vehicle breaks up above 8 g.

fix.text: Lower gLimit so a stays under maxG, and under 8 g.

pass.text: The skin stays cool enough for the material and the cargo.

amber.text: The outside is getting hot. A tougher nose, or a heat shield, helps.

red.text: The skin would burn through, or the cargo would cook. Change the nose, or add a heat shield.

fix.text: Pick a nose that handles heat, or add a heat shield under a big group of engines.

pass.text: Nose temperature stays under maxTempK, and after jettison ½ρv³ stays under maxHeatFlux.

amber.text: Nose T is nearing maxTempK, or a wide cluster is heating the base. After jettison, ½ρv³ must stay under maxHeatFlux.

red.text: thermal when the base-heating index > 1 (more than 9 engines and no heat shield) or nose T > maxTempK. Jettison also needs ½ρv³ < maxHeatFlux.

fix.text: Add a base heat shield, or pick a nose with a higher maxTempK. Keep ½ρv³ under maxHeatFlux after jettison.

pass.text: The legs can take the landing.

amber.text: The landing may be too hard for these legs. Save more fuel, or use stronger legs.

red.text: The legs would fold and the booster would tip over. Use stronger legs, or come down slower.

fix.text: Use stronger legs, or save more fuel so the landing is softer.

pass.text: Touchdown v_z ≤ v_leg. Light legs take 2 m/s. Heavy legs take 4 m/s.

amber.text: v_z is near v_leg (2 m/s light, 4 m/s heavy).

red.text: leg-collapse when v_z > v_leg. Light legs are 2 m/s. Heavy legs are 4 m/s, at +9% dry mass.

fix.text: Use heavy legs (v_leg = 4 m/s), or add landing reserve so v_z falls.

pass.text: This flight is set to come home.

red.text: This mission needs the booster back. Pick a pad or a barge.

fix.text: Choose a landing on the pad, or on a barge at sea.

pass.text: Recovery mode is a pad return or a barge. A pad return needs about 2·v_h m/s.

red.text: Mode is expendable, but the mission requires a landing. A pad return needs ≈ 2·v_h(MECO) m/s. A barge needs ≈ 0.3·v_h.

fix.text: Set recovery to the pad (≈ 2·v_h) or the barge (≈ 0.3·v_h).

pass.text: The landing-fuel check is ready.

amber.text: We don't know the landing fuel yet. You can go on, then check it again.

fix.text: Continue, then look again once the flight preview finishes.

pass.text: Boost-back Δv is cached from horizontal speed at engine cutoff, v_h (m/s).

amber.text: Landing need is unknown until the preview caches v_h. Pad ≈ 2·v_h, barge ≈ 0.3·v_h, in m/s.

fix.text: Wait for the preview flight. Need is 2·v_h for the pad and 0.3·v_h for the barge.

pass.text: Enough fuel is saved for the landing.

red.text: Not enough fuel saved to land. Hold more back, or land closer.

fix.text: Save more fuel for landing, or pick the barge so the trip home is shorter.

pass.text: Landing reserve (m/s) ≥ need. Pad need ≈ 2·v_h. Barge need ≈ 0.3·v_h.

red.text: Reserve < Δv_land. Δv_land ≈ v_term + g·t_burn·(1 − 1/TWR_land), plus the boost-back.

fix.text: Raise the landing reserve, or switch from the pad (≈ 2·v_h) to the barge (≈ 0.3·v_h).

pass.text: The booster has legs for the landing.

amber.text: Fuel is saved for landing, but there are no legs. Add legs, or the booster falls over.

fix.text: Add landing legs.

pass.text: landing.legs is true. Legs add about 6% to first-stage dry mass.

amber.text: A landing is required and landing.legs is false. Without legs there is no v_leg for v_z to meet.

fix.text: Turn on legs. Light legs: v_leg = 2 m/s and +6% dry mass. Heavy: 4 m/s and +9%.

pass.text: The booster can steer itself on the way down.

amber.text: To land, the booster needs little steering jets.

fix.text: Turn on the little steering jets for the way down.

pass.text: Landing steering is on, so M_ctrl exists and CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero can be formed on the way down.

amber.text: Landing fuel is saved and the steering jets are off. CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero needs that moment in the descent.

fix.text: Turn on landing steering so M_ctrl feeds CAR = M_ctrl/M_aero when the bell can no longer point the booster.

skip.text: This flight doesn't need a landing. You can skip bringing it home.

fix.text: Skip is fine. Open this step only if you still want the booster back.

skip.text: The mission does not require landing, so reserve ≥ Δv_land (m/s) is not a gate.

fix.text: Leave it expendable, or pick a landing if you want the ≈ 2·v_h or ≈ 0.3·v_h check.

pass.text: The risk check is still working. Nothing red is on the list yet.

fix.text: Give it a moment, then look again before you fly.

pass.text: The preview flight is not cached yet, so q (kPa) and peak g are not known. Nothing on the list is red.

fix.text: Wait for the preview. The risk list needs that pass before q vs q_lim is real.

pass.text: Every risk on the list has a name.

amber.text: This rocket has a red risk. Look before you launch.

fix.text: Open the risk and use its fix before you fly.

pass.text: Every red row has a failure kind and a margin against its limit, such as q_lim.

amber.text: A red risk arrived without a kind name. Red means a limit is already crossed, such as q > q_lim.

fix.text: Open the row. Red means a trigger is already true, such as q > q_lim or S < 0 with CAR < 1.
